title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: US federal prosecutors say businesses have lost $129M+ to scam calls using AI-generated voices to mimic company executives in the 18 months since July 2024 (Adeel Hassan/New York Times)
items.content_text: US federal prosecutors revealed that over the 18 months since July 2024, three suspects used generative AI to clone executive voices and conduct phone scams. By mimicking the voices of CEOs to manipulate employees into transferring funds, the operation has caused over $129 million in losses to businesses.

items.title: Sources: the EU sues IBM, French IT group Atos, and Italian contractor Leonardo over delays in developing its smart border system, which caused travel chaos (Laura Dubois/Financial Times)
items.content_text: The EU has filed a lawsuit in Estonia against IBM, Atos, and Leonardo for chronic delays in developing its smart border system, which caused widespread travel chaos. The project, designed to upgrade border entry management, suffered from repeated contractor failures, forcing the EU to seek legal recourse for the stalled implementation.

items.title: Chinese media denies Beijing's link to Jensen Huang's affair, accuses the US media of a fabricated spy narrative, and warns the issue may hurt trade relations (Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Beijing has officially dismissed allegations of spying on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, labeling such claims as fabricated narratives by US media. This rebuttal aims to counter accusations of leveraging business leaders for intelligence gathering, while warning that such baseless rhetoric is undermining the foundation of bilateral commercial and trade relations.

items.title: As companies replace human workers with AI agents, determining managers' grade and pay is becoming harder, as both often depend on how many people they manage (Pilita Clark/Financial Times)
items.content_text: As companies accelerate the deployment of AI agents to replace human staff, traditional pay and grading structures are crumbling. Managers who previously tied their compensation to headcounts now face a crisis of definition as HR struggles to quantify the 'span of control' in an era of AI automation.

items.title: Toronto-based Ada and SF-based Dialpad, both makers of AI customer service software, agree to merge in an all-share deal valuing Ada at ~$430M, sources say (Globe and Mail)
items.content_text: Toronto-based Ada has agreed to merge with U.S.-based Dialpad in an all-share deal, valuing the Canadian AI customer service firm at approximately $430 million. Once a unicorn with a $1.2 billion valuation, Ada's market value has plummeted by nearly two-thirds due to the post-pandemic tech correction and market disruption from LLMs.

items.title: Bikers and Bug-Lovers Join Forces to Fight a New Google Data Center
items.content_text: Environmental groups, wildlife advocates, and a motorcycle club protested outside Google’s office, demanding the company abandon a proposed data center development in Thurrock. The protesters cite threats to endangered species, pollution concerns, and the loss of a racing site, as Google ramps up industrial-scale data centers across the UK to satisfy its surging AI compute demand.

items.title: Google rolls out a Googlebook update that frees up 3GB-6GB of RAM via on-device AI optimizations, reduces Chrome crashes, patches ~60 Android flaws, and more (Jay Bonggolto/Android Central)
items.content_text: Google has rolled out a system update optimizing AICore and NPU drivers to reduce memory consumption by background AI processes. This update frees up to 6GB of RAM and enhances system stability, specifically preventing browser crashes during heavy workloads.

items.title: Sources: ByteDance seeks to expand its data center project in Ceara, Brazil, with a second phase larger than its ongoing $10B, 300MW project (Peter Millard/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: ByteDance is considering a second phase expansion for its data center project in Ceara, Brazil. The scale and investment for this phase are expected to exceed the initial $10 billion, 300MW project, signaling a massive push for regional compute infrastructure.

items.title: How Sequoia's Alfred Lin and Pat Grady erased Roelof Botha's legacy, halving GPs and unwinding his fund; sources say he joined SpaceX's board behind their backs (Financial Times)
items.content_text: Sequoia partners Alfred Lin and Pat Grady dismantled Roelof Botha's legacy by closing the London office and unwinding the permanent capital fund. This restructuring followed reports that Botha joined the SpaceX board without internal disclosure, effectively sidelining him.

items.title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno
items.content_text: Rights holders for Elvis Presley and Eminem have filed a joint lawsuit against AI music platform Suno. The plaintiffs allege that Suno uses AI to illegally generate music and lyrics that mimic these artists, specifically accusing the company of violating Tennessee's ELVIS Act by misappropriating their voices and creative labor.

items.title: Andrej Karpathy built a curated video platform in a weekend using Claude and 20 years of Hacker News
items.content_text: AI researcher Andrej Karpathy utilized the Claude model to process 20 years of Hacker News data over a weekend, building an automated video recommendation platform. By relying on Claude Code for nearly all tasks including data analysis and server setup, he demonstrated how advanced AI models can compress projects that previously took weeks into just a few hours.

items.title: The brain-as-computer metaphor shaped modern AI but may be misleading the consciousness debate
items.content_text: Three leading neuroscience experts have jointly published a commentary challenging the notion that current AI systems could be conscious. They argue against the belief that 'correct computations' automatically lead to consciousness, asserting that silicon hardware may lack the necessary foundation for subjective experience, and they express skepticism regarding Anthropic's findings on internal processing patterns.

items.title: I Used NYT Cooking’s New AI-Powered Recipe Modifier, and It’s Actually Pretty Good
items.content_text: NYT Cooking recently launched an AI-powered feature for recipe scaling and unit conversion, aimed at simplifying prep work. Despite intense backlash in the comment section over 'smart kitchen' fatigue, the feature has proven surprisingly reliable and functional in real-world usage.

items.title: The inventor of the bitter lesson has a bitter lesson for LLM scaling enthusiasts
items.content_text: Turing Award winner Richard Sutton argued on social media that raw compute scaling alone won't lead to AGI. He criticized the reliance on synthetic data, advocating for AI agents that move beyond static internet text and learn continuously through complex real-world interactions.

items.title: Inside Inner Mongolia, China's fastest-growing AI data center region, where construction is accelerating with low building cost and no public backlash (SemiAnalysis)
items.content_text: Inner Mongolia's Ulanqab is becoming the epicenter of China's AI infrastructure, with massive gigawatt-scale data center clusters under construction. The region delivers projects at one-fifth the cost of US counterparts with lightning speed, leveraging policy and geographic advantages without the public backlash seen in the West.
